prompts.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: single enemy visual design study for Emergency Shift, a 2D overhead hospital horror game. Make ONE entire creature, centered with comfortable transparent margins, facing toward the TOP of the image. Strict orthographic camera exactly 90 degrees above the creature, looking at its dorsal surface; zero perspective, zero visible side faces, no horizon, no presentation stand, no cast shadow. Hand-painted detailed organic game illustration, controlled broad forms and a restrained amount of anatomical texture, muted flesh palette, thin dark contours. This is a concept, not an animation sheet. Full connected anatomy, all limbs complete and attached, natural restrained asymmetry in joint pose and tissue bands, readable at a tiny game size. Non-human alien flesh, no clothing or gear, no hair, no dog face, no insect carapace, no central giant eye, no neon, no glowing parts, no blood pool, no floor, no motion blur, no text. Actual transparent background. Direction A / TENDON RUNNER, recommended: a narrow elongated teardrop torso, dorsal length about twice torso width, four limbs total. TWO short planted steering forelimbs attached at the front shoulders and TWO long strongly bent spring-like hind legs attached to an enlarged rear pelvic mass; each hind leg has one visibly continuous tendon strut and a compact blunt bone toe. The hind legs trail back and spread just enough to form a clear rear fork. NO tail and NO extra limbs. The front is a small blunt sensory wedge with two subtle dark lateral sensory pits and a closed transverse biting seam visible from above, not a human or animal head. A broad dark longitudinal tendon groove runs along the pale warm gray-beige back; muted wine-red tissue only in a few joint gaps. The top outline must read as a long forward arrow with four distinct running supports and large negative gaps. Depict an asymmetric mid-run contact pose, credible runner pushing from its rear legs, not a leaping frog or a spider.

Four attached running limbs total, two at each end of the crescent, short and powerful with compact blunt pale contact tips. Thick forward rim contains a CLOSED curved biting seam; sensory organs are two small dorsal dimples on the arms of the crescent. No long neck, no tail, no eye in the middle and no triangular central body. The overall outline is broad and transverse, visibly wider than it is long, with a large rear notch that stays readable small. Dusty gray-lilac flesh, desaturated violet tendon bundles, pale gray tips. Distinct organic asymmetry: one arm slightly fuller and one rear leg drawn closer. It should feel like a disturbing muscular organ that RUNS fast along a corridor, not a crab, insect, logo, or machine.

Body length is about 3 times body width; overall footprint including legs is a narrow centipede-like lane runner, but only SIX limbs, no shell or insect segments. All three pairs are visibly attached to one continuous flexible muscle body; alternating contact pose, all limb tips visible with clean dark gaps between them. A blunt forward tip has a short closed biting seam and no face, a tapering rear ends in flesh rather than a tail. Two large offset longitudinal ivory-gray tendon bands on a desaturated umber-gray back make direction readable; small dull burgundy folds only at leg roots, never glowing. Organic and alien, flesh rather than armored arthropod. The visible long-axis body and three-pair cadence should strongly distinguish it from a wide radial six-legged eye creature.
